review_note: Montana's disaster-declaration EOs use the boilerplate title "Declaring a Disaster to Exist in the State of Montana" with no hazard word in the title itself. The governor's-office news release for this order confirms it was issued for flooding in northeast western and south central Montana from snowmelt and rainfall beginning April 10 2023.

Same boilerplate title as MT-EO-1-2023 with no hazard word. Issued three weeks after 1-2023 for continued/renewed flooding conditions; classified from the surrounding news coverage rather than the order title alone.

Same boilerplate title with no hazard word. The governor's-office news release confirms this order responded to flooding in northern and central Montana from heavy rain and snowmelt beginning May 5 2024.

Same boilerplate title with no hazard word. Confirmed via the order's own PDF text (visible in search results) and governor's-office coverage as flooding on the Fisher and Yaak Rivers in northwestern Montana beginning December 8 2025.

The scraper's boilerplate-title check flags this ID for override regardless of trailing text, so the override is recorded even though the parenthetical in event_description already names the hazard. Confirmed via the order's own PDF text: a severe wind event beginning December 17 2025 with gusts over 90 mph and sustained winds near 65 mph across every Montana county.
Title is 'Declaring a Statewide Wildland Fire Emergency' - the classifier's fire keyword requires wildfire/forest fire/brush fire as compound terms specifically, not this phrasing.

Confirmed via the order's own press release: 'harsh winter weather... record breaking cold, and deep snow' delayed propane/heating-oil deliveries, triggering this energy emergency. Titled only 'Energy Emergency' with no weather keyword in the title itself.
Declares a disaster to send Montana resources in support of Washington; no Montana weather event to match.
Declares a disaster to send Montana support to Texas; no Montana weather event to match.
Waives motor carrier rules for vehicles assisting fire suppression; an administrative waiver, not a disaster declaration.
